solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Author protecting pound provided for feral animals

indicators.note: protecting means the author's name wraps around and shelters the other letters

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright and wit
L is the abbreviation for a pound (from Latin libra)
provided, as in 'provided that', means if

explanation.surface: A writer shields money set aside to look after wild creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild animals living untamed in nature are collectively called by this word, so feral creatures fit.

clue.text: Left on charts kept by newest ward sister

indicators.note: kept by means the letters sit held inside the following run of words, across their boundaries

explanation.surface: A hospital note says something on the charts was left by the newest ward sister.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across neWEST WARD Sister. On a map with north at the top, west lies to the left, so 'Left on charts' is a fair direction definition.
explanation.definitionFit: On maps west is to the left, so heading toward the left on a chart means going in that direction.

clue.text: Left part of Europe for part of Africa

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a corner of Europe for a corner of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a West African country, so it is literally a portion of that continent.

clue.text: Priests holding mass for old feast day

indicators.note: holding means the priests' word grips the other letter inside it

parts.note: lamas are Buddhist priests or monks of Tibet
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Clergy celebrating a service on an ancient religious holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Lammas (1 August) was the old English harvest festival, when loaves made from the first wheat were blessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lammas was a traditional English harvest festival on 1 August, a holy day no longer widely kept.

clue.text: Feminine expert on the best kind of cosmetic

parts.note: F is the grammatical abbreviation for feminine
an ace is someone highly skilled
the cream is the finest part, as in 'cream of the crop'

explanation.surface: A woman who knows beauty products recommends the finest one.
explanation.definitionFit: A moisturising lotion applied to the skin of the face is a common cosmetic product.

clue.text: Work on last part of road surface

definitions.meaning: to mend shoes, as a shoemaker does on a last, the foot-shaped block
a rounded stone used in paving old streets

explanation.walkthrough: A last is the shoemaker's foot-shaped mould, not 'final'; the first sense is repairing shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler mends shoes on a last, and a rounded paving stone shares the same name, giving two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Check study on way to fish with single line

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: L stands for line, and leaving only one of the pair removes the other

parts.note: to troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat

explanation.surface: An angler studies the road before fishing with only one line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places the study word first; 'with single line' cuts the doubled L of the fishing word down to one.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to restrain or regulate it, which is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Lead, for example, special team into European city

indicators.note: into means the rearranged letters go inside the city's name

parts.note: Basel is a Swiss city on the Rhine

indicators.note: special here signals the letters of team are made into something different

explanation.surface: A lead player and a special squad travel to a city on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' anagrams the squad word, and 'into' puts it inside the Swiss city. 'Lead' is the metal, not a leading role.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a common non-precious metal, the kind alchemists hoped to turn into gold.

clue.text: Apprentice is more efficient, master finally admitted

indicators.note: admitted means the extra letter is let inside the other word

parts.note: leaner, as in a lean organisation, is more efficient

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word master

explanation.surface: A trainee works more efficiently, the master at last concedes.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone still being trained in a skill, as an apprentice is.

clue.text: Insulting expression, initially, can make one cry

definitions.meaning: the initials of a common crude insult for a person, son of a bitch

explanation.surface: A rude remark, from the very start, may reduce someone to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' says the first sense is an abbreviation formed from the insult's initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for a crude insult shares its spelling with the verb meaning to weep convulsively.

clue.text: Romance is wild round island in part of Pacific

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the other letter
wild signals the letters of romance is run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Love is passionate on a tropical isle in the South Seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges ROMANCE IS around I for island.
explanation.definitionFit: Micronesia is a region of many small islands in the western Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Steps taken in preparation for engagement

definitions.text: Steps taken in preparation for engagement

parts.words: Steps taken in preparation for engagement
parts.note: reads like getting ready to propose marriage, but the steps are dance steps and the engagement is a battle

explanation.walkthrough: The engagement is military, not romantic; the steps are literally danced before fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal warriors performed a ritual dance before battle, the steps preceding a military engagement.

clue.text: Old chap carried by railway, one of those travelling

indicators.note: carried by means the other letters ride inside the railway's abbreviation

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: An elderly man rides on a train, one of the passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Romany are a traditionally nomadic people, so 'one of those travelling' points to a traveller, not a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romany are a traditionally itinerant people, often called travellers in Britain.

clue.text: Doomed king switching sides? True

indicators.note: switching means the letter for one side is exchanged for the other in the king's name
sides points to L and R, the abbreviations for left and right, which trade places

parts.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's tragic hero, dies at the end of the play

explanation.surface: A tragic monarch changes allegiance: is it genuine?
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) and R (right) swap places in LEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something real is genuine or actual, which is what true means here.

clue.text: Overlapping signs showing facilities for readers

indicators.note: overlapping means the two signs share a letter where they join, so it appears only once

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac
Aries is another sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Notices that overlap advertise services for book lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: Two zodiac signs, LIBRA and ARIES, overlap on their shared A.
explanation.definitionFit: Libraries are public buildings provided so people can borrow and read books.

clue.text: Eye-opening article by Conservative party initially

indicators.note: initially says the party word comes first, before the rest

parts.note: a revel is a lively celebration
a is the indefinite article
Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on a Tory party gathering proves illuminating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revelatory discloses surprising truths, so it is eye-opening.

clue.text: Keep in mind, record ain't broken

parts.note: to enter data is to record it

indicators.note: broken means the letters of ain't are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Remember to log it: the slang word isn't proper grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges AINT to TAIN. To entertain an idea is to hold it in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain a thought is to consider or harbour it, keeping it in mind.

clue.text: Measure getting police HQ's mark of approval

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police headquarters
a tick is the check mark showing something is correct

explanation.surface: Something gets the stamp of approval from police headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard, often just 'the Yard', is the London Metropolitan Police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard by which things are judged, a measure.

clue.text: Impasse on board about British colleague in same organization

indicators.note: about means the deadlock word goes around the extra letter

parts.note: stalemate is the chess position where neither side can win

explanation.surface: Deadlock in the boardroom over a British associate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means a chessboard, not a company board: stalemate is a drawn chess position.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablemate is literally a horse from the same stable, figuratively a fellow member of one group.

clue.text: Tourist as person having highly enjoyable experience?

definitions.meaning: someone on a trip in the slang sense, high on drugs

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the slang sense: a trip is a drug-induced high.
explanation.definitionFit: A day visitor to the seaside is one sense; slang for someone high on hallucinogens is the other.

clue.text: Demand payment of levy heartlessly, or in nice way

parts.note: to exact a sum is to demand it

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle of levy is removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Collect a tax without mercy, or in a polite manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nice' is used in its old sense of precise or fine, not pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice can mean precise or subtle, so done in a nice way is done precisely.

clue.text: Landowner hasn't finished making den

indicators.note: hasn't finished means the final letter of the landowner word is dropped

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner

explanation.surface: A property owner has not completed building a hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAIRD is a Scottish landed proprietor.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a wild animal's resting place, a den.

clue.text: Scene of annual US event one month before its start

indicators.note: before puts the month ahead of the next letter

parts.note: August is a month of the year
its start is the first letter of the month just found

explanation.surface: An American event comes round each year, a month before it begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Augusta, Georgia, hosts the Masters golf tournament each April. 'its' refers back to the month, whose opening letter is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta National in Georgia stages the Masters golf tournament every spring.

clue.text: Garment in which King Edward got very hot

definitions.text: in which King Edward got very hot
definitions.meaning: a King Edward is a British potato variety, baked whole in its skin

explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety; a jacket potato is baked in its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A short coat is one sense; a potato baked whole in its skin is said to be cooked in this.

clue.text: I moved in train to a foreign capital

indicators.note: moved says the letter I shifts to a new place within the word train

explanation.surface: I travelled by rail to a capital city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' shifts the I one place within the word train; then A follows. Tirana is the capital of Albania.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirana is the capital city of Albania, foreign from the British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Settles scores

explanation.walkthrough: 'scores' is a verb: to score music is to arrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle matters means to sort them out, and to score music is to adapt it for performers.

clue.text: Bluntly indicate financial institution must protect pound

parts.note: to point is to indicate

indicators.note: must protect means the bank's letters enclose the other letter

parts.note: a bank is a financial institution

explanation.surface: Indicate frankly that a bank has to safeguard sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking point-blank means speaking directly and without softening, bluntly.

clue.text: Way to address some respected Indian, originally

definitions.text: Way to address some respected Indian, originally

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A form of address for an esteemed person in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of Some Respected Indian give the honorific, which is itself a respectful title in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri is an Indian honorific placed before the name of a respected person.

clue.text: Playful female — dangerous, too

parts.note: risky means dangerous

explanation.surface: A lively woman who is also hazardous company.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky describes someone lively and full of high spirits, playful.

clue.text: Part of record for monomaniac

definitions.meaning: a single song or piece on an album
obsessed with only one thing, as in a narrow mind

explanation.walkthrough: A one-track mind thinks about only one subject.
explanation.definitionFit: One song on an album is one sense; an obsessive mind fixed on a single subject is the other.
